open_points.subject: FlowEdge guard propagation into constant-fed inputs
open_points.text: “A node one of whose input ports has every incoming edge disabled by its guard, or coming from a skipped node, is not executed” conflicts with FlowConstant being “delivered to one input port like any other value.”
open_points.question: When an input port is supplied by a FlowConstant, does that constant count as an available input that prevents the port from causing `skipped_by_guard`, even though the rule speaks only of incoming edges?
options: A delivered constant prevents that input port from causing the skip
A constant-fed port with no incoming edges satisfies the every-incoming-edge condition and causes the skip
Constants participate in the condition under a separate rule
open_points.default_guess: Treat a delivered constant as satisfying the input port, so it does not cause `skipped_by_guard`.

open_points.subject: FlowEdge guard skipping of mapped nodes
open_points.text: “A node one of whose input ports has every incoming edge disabled by its guard, or coming from a skipped node, is not executed and is recorded `skipped_by_guard`” does not say whether “a node” means the whole mapped node or one execution identified by `map_index`.
open_points.question: For a mapped node whose guard availability differs between elements, is `skipped_by_guard` decided independently for each `map_index`, or does one skipped input condition skip the whole mapped node?
options: Decide separately for each mapped element, allowing succeeded and skipped executions for one node
Skip the entire mapped node if the condition holds for any element
Require the condition to hold for every element before skipping the entire node

open_points.subject: NodeExecution status when guard-skipped and failed dependencies coexist
open_points.text: M15 says a node is recorded `skipped_by_guard` when one input port has all sources disabled or skipped, while M23 says a node not executed because “an upstream node failed” is recorded `upstream_failed`.
open_points.question: Which status is recorded when one input port meets the new `skipped_by_guard` condition but another input depends on a failed node?
options: The proof must exclude graphs where both reasons can apply
A separate status or multiple records represent both reasons
open_points.default_guess: Record `upstream_failed`, because an actual failed dependency is the stronger cause preventing execution.
